1	# TRUST_ASSUMPTIONS.md
2	
3	What the Verity port of the PQSigner smart-wallet contracts **does and
4	does not** verify. Matches Verity's own convention
5	([`lfglabs-dev/verity/TRUST_ASSUMPTIONS.md`](https://github.com/lfglabs-dev/verity/blob/main/TRUST_ASSUMPTIONS.md)).
6	
7	A default `lake build` compiles only the eight pure-Lean **Part B** modules.
8	It does **not** build `Theorems.lean` or establish any Part A wallet obligation.
9	Part A imports APIs absent from the pinned Verity release and remains unverified.
10	
11	`make verify-verity-census` freshly compiles all eight Part B modules with pinned
12	Lean 4.22.0 and inventories their exported declarations (including private and
13	generated declarations). It checks every declaration's transitive axiom closure,
14	not just theorem names or source keywords. Before the census, a separate
15	lean4checker kernel replay validates all 208 safe, non-partial Part B constants
16	against a separate environment imported from the pinned Lean distribution.
17	Constructors/recursors are compared with kernel-generated metadata. The five
18	existing partial compiler helpers are inventoried but excluded from replay;
19	unsafe project declarations are rejected. Ordinary `.olean` imports alone do
20	not recheck declarations added with kernel checking disabled.
21	
22	The checked baseline contains 15
23	environment axioms, of which two are project axioms, and one admitted Part B
24	helper: `PQSigner.Verifier.Merkle.yul_swap_selector_in_known_set`. Its name,
25	statement and admitted body are pinned; new dependents cannot inherit that
26	exception. A proof discharging the same statement is allowed.
27	
28	The five unbuildable Part A sources are instead pinned byte-for-byte. Their
29	11 source holes and CREATE2 axiom are **uncompiled, unverified obligations**.
30	Changing that quarantine or any census allowance requires an explicit reviewed
31	baseline change. The raw per-file hole count remains an additional backstop.
32	
33	The installed pinned Lean compiler, standard library, Python gate and reviewed
34	baseline are trusted. This is an exported-environment census, not an independent
35	kernel implementation, audit of transient anonymous examples, or proof of
36	Rust/Yul/Solidity equivalence. Lake caches and Part A cannot supply proof evidence
37	to this gate. See `assurance_inventory.json` for exact identities and hashes.
38	
39	## Part A intended obligations — not verified
40	
41	| Theorem | Statement | Implies CLAUDE.md invariant |
42	|---------|-----------|------------------------------|
43	| #1, #2, #3 | All three counter writers are monotonic and bounded by their caps. | #7 (per-chain caps monotonic) |
44	| #4 | `_removeOwnerAtIndex(0, _)` always reverts. | #6 (bootstrap immutable) — part 1 |
45	| #5 | No reachable trace overwrites `ownerAtIndex[0]` after construction. | #6 (bootstrap immutable) — part 2 |
46	| #6 | N-mask layout is enforced for every owner add. | (no CLAUDE.md mapping; defence-in-depth) |
47	| #7 | Factory salt has zero data dependence on `chainId`. | #6 (same address every chain) |
48	| #8 | `createAccount` is idempotent given identical args. | (no CLAUDE.md mapping; safety) |
49	| #9 | Distinct `chainId` ⇒ distinct squat-defence digest. | Squat-defence cross-chain |
50	| #10 | `ownerIndex == 0` dispatch only bumps `bootstrapUses`, only allows `addOwnerBytes`. | Dispatch correctness |
51	| #11 | `ownerIndex ≥ 1` dispatch never bumps `bootstrapUses`. | Dispatch correctness |
52	| #12 | EIP-1271 rejects `ownerIndex == 0`. | Bootstrap key never EIP-1271-signs |
53	| #13 | Global combined-cap invariant. | #7 (combined invariant) |
54	
55	## What is NOT verified (trusted axioms)
56	
57	> **Source axiom census (issue #673):** the tree declares exactly
58	> **3 `axiom`s** — `sha256_size` + `sha256_deterministic`
59	> (`PQSigner/Verifier/Hash.lean:40,47`; item 2 below) and
60	> **`predict_matches_create`** (`PQSigner/PQSmartWalletFactory.lean:65`;
61	> item 4 below — a content-bearing CREATE2 address-prediction claim, not
62	> merely a call-shape bridge). Only the Hash pair is elaborated by the Part B
63	> gate; the factory axiom is covered by the unverified Part A source quarantine.
64	
65	1. **`SPHINCsC10Asm.sol` correctness.** Modelled as opaque oracle
66	   `c10Verify : ByteVec → ByteVec → ByteVec → ByteVec → Bool`. We
67	   assume:
68	   - Deterministic in its inputs.
69	   - May revert (caller wraps in `try/catch`).
70	   - No observable side effect on our ERC-7201 namespace.
71	
72	   The verifier itself implements FIPS 205-aligned SPHINCS+C10 in
73	   hand-tuned Yul. Lifting this to a Lean theorem is the subject of
74	   `docs/archive/handoff-verity-c10-verifier.md`.
75	
76	2. **SHA-256 / Keccak-256 precompile correctness.** Both are
77	   axiomatised as the spec hash functions. Theorem #9
78	   (`addSlot0Digest_binds_chain_id`) relies on SHA-256
79	   collision-resistance — that is an assumption on the function, not
80	   a Lean-provable fact.
81	
82	3. **`solc 0.8.33` Yul → EVM bytecode correctness.** Verity's
83	   in-Lean compilation proof terminates at Yul; the Yul → bytecode
84	   lowering is `solc`. Pinning the version (matching Verity's own
85	   pin) is our only mitigation. Verity itself acknowledges this in
86	   its TRUST_ASSUMPTIONS.md.
87	
88	4. **Solady `LibClone` (`createDeterministicERC1967`,
89	   `predictDeterministicAddressERC1967`).** Axiomatised by:
90	
91	   ```lean
92	   axiom predict_matches_create :
93	     ∀ impl salt factory value,
94	       (createDeterministicERC1967 value impl salt factory).fst =
95	         predictDeterministicAddressERC1967 impl salt factory
96	   ```
97	
98	   The deeper claim — that the resulting address equals
99	   `CREATE2(factory, salt, ERC1967_INIT_CODE_HASH(impl))` — is a
100	   property of Solady's lib + the EVM CREATE2 opcode + `keccak256`.
101	   Out of scope.
102	
103	5. **EIP-1967 proxy `delegatecall` semantics.** All wallets are
104	   ~55-byte proxies that `DELEGATECALL` to the impl. We reason about
105	   the impl directly; the proxy is opaque and assumed semantics-
106	   preserving (this is a property of `DELEGATECALL` + EIP-1967, not
107	   our code).
108	
109	6. **EntryPoint v0.6 invariants.** The caller of `validateUserOp` is
110	   the EntryPoint singleton. We axiomatise that it follows ERC-4337
111	   v0.6 — specifically that it never calls `validateUserOp` with
112	   stale `missingAccountFunds` or skips the post-call settlement.
113	   Out of scope; trusted per the ERC-4337 spec.
114	
115	7. **Firmware-side wire format from CLAUDE.md §"Unified sign
116	   input".** The SHA-256 preimage that the firmware signs is *input*
117	   to our spec (via the opaque `sphincsDigest` function), not
118	   verified by it. If the firmware's `cmd_sign_userop.rs` builds the
119	   wrong preimage, the sigs it produces will be rejected on-chain —
120	   fail-safe, but the bug is not caught here.
121	
122	8. **`block.chainid` truthfulness.** The "same 24 words → same
123	   address on every chain" claim holds within a single canonical
124	   history per chain. An L2 reorg that retroactively reassigns its
125	   chain ID is out of scope (and would be a far larger problem than
126	   our wallet).
127	
128	9. **Gas griefing / OOG.** Verity does not reason about gas. The C10
129	   verify burns 1.7–4M gas; an attacker who supplies a malformed
130	   UserOp that triggers an OOG before the counter bump could leave
131	   storage in a stuck-pending state. Mitigation lives at the
132	   EntryPoint level (bundler gas estimation) and at the firmware
133	   level (slot-cache invalidation on OOG), not in this Lean proof.
134	
135	10. **`bumpBootstrapUses` is never called outside `validateUserOp`.**
136	    The chain of custody from "external entry point" to "counter
137	    bump" is part of theorem #10. If a future PR exposes
138	    `_bumpBootstrapUses` as a public function (or adds a new public
139	    entry point that calls it), theorem #10's premise no longer
140	    holds — but Lean would not catch it, because the new entry point
141	    is a new theorem obligation. **Code review remains responsible
142	    for noticing new public writers.**
143	
144	## Recovering trust when an axiom fails
145	
146	Each axiom corresponds to a specific failure mode:
147	
148	| Axiom failure | What breaks | Mitigation |
149	|---------------|-------------|------------|
150	| C10 verifier accepts a forged sig | Funds drainable from any slot | Part B handoff (Verity port of `SPHINCsC10Asm.sol`) |
151	| `keccak256` collision found | EIP-712 / CREATE2 collisions across the ecosystem | Industry-wide problem; out of scope |
152	| `sha256` collision found | Squat-defence digest reuse across chains | Industry-wide; out of scope. The combined-cap invariant still holds. |
153	| `solc 0.8.33` codegen bug | Verified Yul → buggy EVM bytecode | Differential test against the existing Solidity build catches behavioural divergence on test vectors |
154	| Solady `LibClone` deploys at wrong address | CREATE2 prediction differs from actual deploy | Solady is audited; if their pin moves, re-validate |
155	| EntryPoint v0.6 violates ERC-4337 | UserOp settlement breaks | Industry-wide; out of scope |
156	| Firmware builds wrong `sphincsDigest` preimage | Sigs rejected on-chain (fail-safe) | Firmware-side test in `secure/src/nsc/cmd_sign_userop.rs` |
157	
158	## Diff against `lfglabs-dev/verity/TRUST_ASSUMPTIONS.md`
159	
160	Verity's own list:
161	- Lean kernel correctness (trusted)
162	- `solc` Yul-to-bytecode correctness (trusted)
163	- `lake` build reproducibility (trusted)
164	
165	Our additions:
166	- C10 verifier (opaque oracle — the big one)
167	- Solady `LibClone` (axiomatised)
168	- EntryPoint v0.6 (axiomatised)
169	- Firmware-side wire format (input to spec)
170	
171	Our list inherits Verity's; the union is what reviewers should look
172	at before declaring a deployment "verified".

11	/-!
12	# `Lean.Environment.replay`
13	
14	`replay env constantMap` will "replay" all the constants in `constantMap : HashMap Name ConstantInfo` into `env`,
15	sending each declaration to the kernel for checking.
16	
17	`replay` does not send constructors or recursors in `constantMap` to the kernel,
18	but rather checks that they are identical to constructors or recursors generated in the environment
19	after replaying any inductive definitions occurring in `constantMap`.
20	
21	`replay` can be used either as:
22	* a verifier for an `Environment`, by sending everything to the kernel, or
23	* a mechanism to safely transfer constants from one `Environment` to another.
24	
25	## Implementation notes
26	
27	This is a patched version of `Lean.Environment.Replay`, which is in the `lean4` repository
28	up to `v4.18.0`, but will be deprecated in `v4.19.0` and then removed. Once it it removed,
29	the prime on the `Replay'` namespace, the prime on `Lean.Environment.replay'`
30	should be removed here.
31	
32	-/

34	namespace Lean.Environment
35	
36	namespace Replay'
37	
38	structure Context where
39	  newConstants : Std.HashMap Name ConstantInfo
40	
41	structure State where
42	  env : Kernel.Environment
43	  remaining : NameSet := {}
44	  pending : NameSet := {}
45	  postponedConstructors : NameSet := {}
46	  postponedRecursors : NameSet := {}

48	abbrev M := ReaderT Context <| StateRefT State IO

50	/-- Check if a `Name` still needs processing. If so, move it from `remaining` to `pending`. -/
51	def isTodo (name : Name) : M Bool := do
52	  let r := (← get).remaining
53	  if r.contains name then
54	    modify fun s => { s with remaining := s.remaining.erase name, pending := s.pending.insert name }
55	    return true
56	  else
57	    return false
58	
59	/-- Use the current `Environment` to throw a `Kernel.Exception`. -/
60	def throwKernelException (ex : Kernel.Exception) : M Unit := do
61	  throw <| .userError <| (← ex.toMessageData {} |>.toString)
62	
63	/-- Add a declaration, possibly throwing a `Kernel.Exception`. -/
64	def addDecl (d : Declaration) : M Unit := do
65	  match (← get).env.addDeclCore 0 d (cancelTk? := none) with
66	  | .ok env => modify fun s => { s with env := env }
67	  | .error ex => throwKernelException ex

69	mutual

71	Check if a `Name` still needs to be processed (i.e. is in `remaining`).
72	
73	If so, recursively replay any constants it refers to,
74	to ensure we add declarations in the right order.
75	
76	The construct the `Declaration` from its stored `ConstantInfo`,
77	and add it to the environment.
78	-/
79	partial def replayConstant (name : Name) : M Unit := do
80	  if ← isTodo name then
81	    let some ci := (← read).newConstants[name]? | unreachable!
82	    replayConstants ci.getUsedConstantsAsSet
83	    -- Check that this name is still pending: a mutual block may have taken care of it.

88	      | .thmInfo    info =>
89	        addDecl (Declaration.thmDecl    info)
90	      | .axiomInfo  info =>

92	      | .opaqueInfo info =>

94	      | .inductInfo info =>

98	        for o in all do

101	        let ctorInfo ← all.mapM fun ci => do
102	          pure (ci, ← ci.inductiveVal!.ctors.mapM fun n => do
103	            pure ((← read).newConstants[n]!))
104	        -- Make sure we are really finished with the constructors.
105	        for (_, ctors) in ctorInfo do
106	          for ctor in ctors do
107	            replayConstants ctor.getUsedConstantsAsSet
108	        let types : List InductiveType := ctorInfo.map fun ⟨ci, ctors⟩ =>
109	          { name := ci.name
110	            type := ci.type

161	or if there are malformed recursors or constructors for inductive types.

163	def replay' (newConstants : Std.HashMap Name ConstantInfo) (env : Environment) : IO Environment := do

166	    -- We skip unsafe constants, and also partial constants.

175	      checkPostponedRecursors
